thread:
morgan: FYI — getting multiple support tickets from customers in us-east reporting SSE streams that cut off mid-response. Symptoms: partial tokens, client sees EventSource 'error' then 1006 close. Start time ~ 11:42 UTC.
keiko: Which customers? any tier pattern?
morgan: A mixture — some PLG free accounts and one enterprise (acme-inc). All using streaming endpoint /v1/streams with model=gpt-eco. Correlation IDs: 81f3... and 9b2d... included in tickets.
eli: Seeing spikes on our fanout workers in us-east-1. Error rate up ~4x for SSE connections. Edge logs show 502s and intermittent 401s (token validation). Possibly auth service instability + downstream fanout overload.
tara: 401s could be token expiry insider loops — are clients getting 401 then reconnecting quickly? Could cause thundering reconnections.
support-bot: From acme-inc logs pasted in ticket: "EventSource: failed to parse SSE frame, connection closed" followed by repeated reconnects every 1s x10.
keiko: Can we reproduce? any simple curl/js snippet? I'll try from curl in region.
morgan: Repro steps from a user (simplified):
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
       -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
       "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=gpt-eco&stream=true" 
User reported seeing first chunk then connection abruptly close.
eli: I spun up an EventSource test from a us-east instance and saw same: first data event, then socket closed with 1006. Edge returned 502 4xx trace logged: "upstream prematurely closed connection". Stack trace hints at worker oom/killed.
keiko: Any changes deployed in last hour? eng-releases shows a small kernel patch pushed to runtime around 11:30 UTC but rollout limited to canary. Not sure it matches region.
ops-bot: Alert: fanout-proxy-us-east CPU at 92% on node fanout-3 (removing node due to healthcheck failures).
morgan: Ok mitigation plan suggestion:
  1) Scale fanout pool in us-east by +2 nodes immediately (autoscale didn't kick).
  2) Temporarily disable cross-zone fanout to reduce copies (set env FANOUT_STRATEGY=single)
  3) Enable non-streaming fallback for impacted customers (X-Redwood-Fallback: chunked) and advise clients to reconnect with longpoll
  4) Add temporary 5s jitter backoff on reconnect behavior for clients via client-side note in status page.
eli: I'm scaling fanout pool now and setting FANOUT_STRATEGY=single on the canary group. Rolling to rest of us-east in 5m pending metrics.
tara: For auth 401s — I traced to our token-issuer cache expiry table: memcached eviction at ~11:40 due to load. Re-priming cache should stop 401s. I'm increasing memcached capacity and raising TTL for token validation keys.
keiko: Can we enable idempotent-session dedupe to avoid double billing when clients reconnect mid-stream? We had a bug where reconnects generated duplicate usage events.
morgan: The billing team suggests using session_id header (X-Redwood-Session) as dedupe key. We can enable dedupe-mode=session in the eventing pipeline for us-east for next 30m. That will prevent duplicated meter events on reconnections.
support-bot: Noted — acme-inc flagged billing spikes for two sessions correlated with those reconnections.
eli: After scale and strategy flip: fanout cpu down to 55% and error rate reduced 80% for active tests. Early customers report streams now persist. Still seeing a couple 502-> reconnect loops for legacy clients.
keiko: Patching memcached and increasing capacity done. No further 401s seen in the last 7m.
morgan: Temporary status update for customers: "We mitigated a streaming degradation in US-East. If you experienced partial stream outputs or unexpected disconnects, please try reconnecting; we enabled a longpoll fallback and deduped billing for affected sessions. Root cause investigation ongoing." I'll post to statuspage and CSL.
tara: Action items logged:
  - eli: follow up to validate fanout worker memory leak hypothesis (heap dump + pprof)
  - keiko: postmortem owner and timeline (assign to tara)
  - morgan: coordinate status page and customer replies
  - infra: confirm autoscale policy fix so pool grows above 2 nodes automatically
ops-bot: Deploy loggroup: /services/fanout/us-east — increased retention 14d. Incident ticket created: INC-2026-4893.
eli: Quick debug note: sample client workaround for JS EventSource to avoid tight reconnect storms:
  const es = new EventSource(url)
  es.onerror = (e) => {
    es.close();
    setTimeout(() => new EventSource(url), Math.floor(Math.random()*4000)+2000);
  }
morgan: Also added server-side header X-Redwood-Conn-ID in responses for easier correlation. Please include that when you paste logs.
keiko: I'm going to toggle a feature flag to enable dedupe-mode=session for us-east now. morgan, confirm with billing once done.
morgan: Confirmed. dedupe-mode=session enabled at 11:58 UTC. Billing team will reconcile later. Posting status note now.
support-bot: acme-inc confirmed streams resumed and billing appears correct for their test sessions. :thumbsup:
eli: Monitoring for 30m. If no regression, we'll roll the strategy change to the other fanout groups and revert canary-specific flags.
tara: Will own the postmortem doc and set P1->P2 after initial RCA. Rough hypothesis: fanout worker resource pressure + token cache eviction + client reconnect storm amplified the outage.
morgan: Closing thread for now — keep updates here. If you see related tickets, tag this incident (INC-2026-4893) and include X-Redwood-Conn-ID. Thanks all.
